html:
The Gangulu, also written Kangulu or Ghungalu, are an Aboriginal Australian people of central Queensland, from the area of today's Woorabinda, Duaringa and Mount Morgan, in the Fitzroy River basin.

Their neighbours were the Darumbal around Rockhampton, the Wadjigu and Garingbal inland, and the Bayali toward the coast.

Gold found at Mount Morgan in 1882 made it one of the richest mines in the world. In the 1920s the Queensland government opened the Woorabinda settlement on Gangulu land, and moved people from many groups there.
sum: The Gangulu, also written Kangulu or Ghungalu, are an Aboriginal Australian people of central Queensland, from the area of today's Woorabinda, Duaringa and Mount Morgan, in the Fitzroy River basin.
